newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Nordics stressing support for Baltics' EU talks.
newsitem.headline: Nordics stressing support for Baltics' EU talks.

text.p: Nordic ministers reiterated on Wednesday that the three Baltic republics should start European Union membership negotiations at the same time as other eastern European applicant countries.
They held discussions with ministers from Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania during a meeting of the Nordic Council of Ministers in Brussels.
Among other things, they discussed relations with the EU, which groups three of the five Nordic states.

"In this respect we will have to stress from the Nordic ministers that we would also like them to start the negotiations at the same time as other countries," Norwegian Industrial Affairs Minister Grete Knudsen told a press conference.
The Nordic Council of Ministers has in operation a series of programmes to help the Baltics in the fields of, for example, education and culture and in helping them prepare for EU accession.
Knudsen, chairing the meeting, said the Council had developed a "working plan" for the Baltics, which also had been discussed during the meeting.
Estonian Foreign Affairs Minister Toomas Ilves said the meeting took "considerable steps in making our cooperation more concrete than it has been."
Asked about relations with neighbouring Russia, Latvian Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs said they had developed in a positive direction, referring to recent border negotiations.

But, he said, Latvia was not happy with a "recently announced document" in Russia about long-term strategy towards the Baltic states. He said there were positive things in the paper but also items which Latvia could not accept, without going into details.
However, he did not want to complain, "because we are in the process of solving problems."
